newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Colonial NZ details fund returns for Jan 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colonial NZ details fund returns for Jan 1997.

text.p: Colonial Investments New Zealand said on Tuesday that January was a quiet month for New Zealand assets, with the sharemarket rising a moderate 1.15 percent and the 10 year government bond yield ending slightly higher at 7.35 percent.
It said the rally in short term rates, which began in October, slowed at the end of January.

Offshore market performance had been volatile, with the Japanese market plunging over 11 percent in the first week of the year and seesawing through the following weeks to end the month just over 5.0 percent down.
However, the United States sharemarket had performed very well, the Dow Jones index rising 5.7 percent.
Major European markets were also strong, with exporters' shares boosted by the rise in the U.S. dollar.

Colonial said no asset allocation changes had been made during January. The following table shows returns on Colonial NZ's managed and sector unit funds for January 1997 and for the 12 months to January 31.
Returns are expressed as a percentage and are net of tax.
Index returns for sector funds are those achieved by the relevant market index. Index returns for managed funds are those based on benchmark asset allocation.
